title: Apical dendrite shape did not predict orientation tuning in 1,524 to 3,779 MICrONS mouse L2/3 neurons; two small-sample claims of Weiler et al. 2022 did not replicate
abstract: Question: does dendrite shape predict orientation tuning in mouse visual cortex? Weiler et al. (2022) reconstructed about 30 L2/3 pyramidal cells. They reported that the apical tree is elongated along the preferred orientation after retinotopic mapping (cc = 0.5), and that sharply tuned cells have less complex apical trees (r = 0.58 with tuning width). We tested both claims in the MICrONS mouse, which has in vivo two-photon tuning and an electron-microscopy reconstruction for each cell (12,829 coregistered neurons, v661 skeletons). We calibrated the image-frame conventions from the digital twin responses. We mapped each apical axis to visual space with a local retinotopic fit and compared it with the preferred bar orientation against shuffle nulls. Result for C1: in 1,524 tuned excitatory V1 L2/3 cells, the alignment was not above the null (mean cos 2 delta 0.050; within-scan null 0.078, p = 0.083; local null 0.055, p = 0.73). All 15 variants were inside or below the null range, and the signed one-axis test went in the opposite direction. Result for C2: in 3,779 V1 L2/3 cells, apical Sholl peak did not predict in vivo gOSI (rho 0.007; r 95% CI -0.015 to 0.049; depth- and scan-adjusted slope -0.021, CI -0.055 to 0.036). Other areas, layers and complexity measures gave the same result. In random 30-cell subsets, |r| >= 0.58 occurred in 0.12% of draws. Limitations: one mouse; most skeletons are automated. A post hoc proofread subset (136 cells, mostly higher visual areas) gave a weak trend in the Weiler direction (rho -0.27; adjusted slope -0.19, p = 0.13) that is not resolved. Unproofread cells with complete-looking apical trees (n = 2,589) were null. The tuning stimulus was Monet noise, not gratings.

display.caption: C1. (a) Absolute angle between the apical long axis (mapped to visual space) and the in vivo preferred bar orientation, for 1,524 tuned V1 L2/3 cells, against a spatially local shuffle band. There is no excess near 0 degrees. (b) Excess mean cos 2 delta over the shuffle null for all 15 alignment tests (grey: null 95% range). (c) The Weiler-style circular-linear statistic in random 30-cell subsets of our cells; 2.4% reach the reported 0.5 (orange). The full-sample value is 0.06 (blue).

C2. (a) In vivo gOSI against apical peak Sholl crossings for 3,779 V1 L2/3 cells (mean and 95% CI; n per bin). (b) Standardized slopes with spatial block-bootstrap 95% CIs for all complexity tests, against the Weiler-sized correlation (orange). (c) Pearson r in random 30-cell subsets; |r| >= 0.58 occurs in 0.12% of draws.

Positive controls. (a) Apical length in L1 falls with soma depth (rho -0.79), so the automated skeleton features carry real structure. (b) In vivo and digital-twin gOSI agree (rho 0.77). (c) Receptive-field azimuth follows mediolateral cortical position in V1 (median local R2 0.52).
